summary: Backend-only testing for SteelTrack iteration 4 (reorder suggestions, field-level history, role-based rate visibility). Created /app/backend/tests/test_steeltrack_iter4_features.py with 10 tests across 3 classes. All 10 iter_4 tests PASS. Full regression (iter_1 + iter_2 + iter_3 + iter_4) = 71/72 pass; the only failure is the already-flagged iter_2 flaky test TestAnalyticsSummary::test_analytics_reflects_new_inward (parallel-worker inward inflation — not a product bug, documented in iter_3). Coverage: (A) Analytics low_stock items include avg_weekly_pcs, weeks_remaining, suggested_reorder_pcs; (A1) zero-outward group => avg_weekly_pcs=0, weeks_remaining=None, suggested_reorder_pcs>=0; (A2) inward=5 + outward=4 in 28d, available=1 => avg_weekly_pcs==1.0 and weeks_remaining==1.0; (A3) low_stock sorted by weeks_remaining ascending, nulls last. (B) PATCH /entries/{id}/office appends one history item per changed tracked field (invoice_no, party_name, rate, payment_terms, office_remarks) with full shape {field, old, new, by, by_name, by_role, at}; (B1) unchanged fields NOT pushed (re-sending same values leaves history untouched); (B2) three sequential PATCHes stacking party_name produce 3 chronological history rows with correct old→new chains; (B3) history field present (empty by default) on both GET /entries and GET /entries/{id}. (C) Labour's GET /entries/{id} returns rate=null even when office set rate=123.45 — admin+office re-read still returns 123.45 (DB untouched); (C1) labour's GET /entries list strips rate on every item; (C2) labour's own POST /entries/inward response has rate=null.

minor.issue: Rate hiding is applied in _enrich_entry via mutation; CSV export (/api/entries.csv) is admin/office-only so unaffected, but if labour ever gets export access the CSV writer must also honour role hiding. Noted for future-proofing only.

history.at is serialised as a native datetime by FastAPI; downstream JSON contains an ISO-8601 string with 'T' separator — tests pass but value is timezone-aware UTC. If frontend parses with Date() this is fine; worth documenting the format in API docs.

action_items: No functional fixes required for iter_4 — all 9 review-request bullets pass.

(Carried from iter_2/iter_3) server.py is now ~1425 lines — split into routers (auth, entries, inventory, analytics, voice, vision, reports, settings) before next iteration; the 700-line soft cap is well exceeded.

(Carried) Analytics endpoint has no RBAC — any logged-in user can view totals + low_stock + reorder suggestions. If reorder/weekly-consumption data is considered pricing-adjacent, confirm labour should see it. (Spec for iter_4 does not require hiding it, so no change made.)
(Carried) Decide whether to update seeded office/admin/labour emails from *@steeltrack.com to Resend-deliverable addresses for manual demos of the party-statement email flow.
Optional: harden iter_2 flaky test TestAnalyticsSummary::test_analytics_reflects_new_inward by filtering delta on created_by (avoid cross-worker inflation).
critical_code_review_comments: History push is correctly guarded: _OFFICE_HISTORY_FIELDS iterated only over keys present in `update` (which already excludes Nones via dict-comp on body.dict()), and old_val != new_val short-circuits identical writes — matches 'unchanged fields must NOT be pushed'.

Rate hiding is centralised in _enrich_entry(e, viewer) which runs on list, detail, create-inward, create-outward and patch responses — single source of truth, so adding new entry endpoints must keep calling it.
Analytics weekly average uses pcs/4.0 over a 28-day window. For a group with outward=4 in 28d: weekly=1.0 — matches spec. For avail=1 and weekly=1.0, weeks_remaining=1.0 — matches spec. Correct.

Low-stock sort key: `(weeks_remaining or 999, pieces_available)` is a simple nulls-last trick. It works because weeks_remaining values for real groups will realistically be < 999. Prefer a sentinel like math.inf or an explicit (is_none, value) tuple for robustness.
server.py has crossed 1400 lines. Split threshold (700) is 2x exceeded. Still strongly recommended to modularise.
No new RBAC bypass surface introduced; office+admin remain the only roles permitted on PATCH /entries/{id}/office.

success_rate.backend: 100% iter_4 (10/10); 98.6% regression (71/72, 1 known-flaky iter_2 test unrelated to iter_4)

seed_data_creation: Tests create short-lived inward/outward entries with ITER4_* grades for isolation. No cleanup — safe on isolated preview DB. No new users created.

flaky_tests.issue: Carries over from iter_3 report. Delta assertion ~157 kg vs other parallel workers' inwards inflating totals (saw 163.28 this run). Not a product bug — tighten by filtering on created_by in future.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env. Seeded users unchanged. iter_4 adds field-level history on PATCH /entries/{id}/office — history[] is cumulative, chronological, one row per changed tracked field (invoice_no, party_name, rate, payment_terms, office_remarks). Labour viewing any entry sees rate=null (applied in _enrich_entry); admin/office still see real rate; DB value is NOT altered. Analytics low_stock items now carry avg_weekly_pcs (pcs over 28d / 4), weeks_remaining (available/weekly, null if weekly==0), suggested_reorder_pcs. low_stock is sorted by weeks_remaining asc, nulls last. server.py is now ~1425 lines; next iteration should split it. For email-triggering tests continue to use delivered@resend.dev (resend rejects *@steeltrack.com).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no new bugs. The single regression failure (iter_2 analytics delta) is a known flaky test due to pytest-xdist parallelism, not a product defect; already documented in iter_3 report.
